note:
emptyparagraphkiller provides ONE text-format filter plugin (id 'emptyparagraphkiller', 'Empty Paragraph filter', type TYPE_TRANSFORM_REVERSIBLE, extends FilterBase) that strips empty

tags (whitespace/  only) from rendered output, non-destructively. No settings form, no schema, no permissions, no Drush, no plugin types (configure=null). Its only state is whether the filter is enabled (and its weight) on a text format, stored in filter.format. under filters.emptyparagraphkiller (status, weight). Medium cases create text formats with the filter on/off and the agent reads filter.format.* config; hard cases enable the filter on / create a text format with the filter, verified against the live filter.format config. Facts grounded in src/Plugin/Filter/EmptyParagraphKiller.php (regex #]*>(\s| ?)*

#) and README.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal 'Empty Paragraph Killer' (emptyparagraphkiller) module do, and how do I switch it on?
evals.expected_output:
It provides a text-format filter that non-destructively removes empty

paragraphs (whitespace/  only) from rendered output. Enable it at /admin/config/content/formats by editing a text format and checking 'Empty paragraph filter'.

evals.prompt: For the emptyparagraphkiller module, what is the filter plugin id and what filter type is it (e.g. how does it behave in the filter pipeline)?
evals.expected_output: The filter plugin id is 'emptyparagraphkiller' (title 'Empty Paragraph filter'), extending FilterBase with type FilterInterface::TYPE_TRANSFORM_REVERSIBLE. prepare() swaps empty paragraphs for a [empty-para] placeholder and process() removes it, so the source is never altered.

evals.prompt: Where in a text format's filter processing order should I place the Empty paragraph killer filter, and why?
evals.expected_output: Per the maintainers, place Empty paragraph killer at (or near) the bottom of the Filter processing order so other filters run first, unless you know a later filter must process its output.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a text format with machine name 'epk_known'. Inspect its live configuration and tell me the id of the filter plugin that is enabled on it.
evals.expected_output: The enabled filter is 'emptyparagraphkiller' — filter.format.epk_known has filters.emptyparagraphkiller.status = true.

evals.prompt: This site has two text formats, 'epk_on' and 'epk_off'. Exactly one of them strips empty paragraphs with the emptyparagraphkiller filter. Inspect the live filter configuration and tell me which format has it enabled.
evals.expected_output: epk_on has the emptyparagraphkiller filter enabled (filter.format.epk_on -> filters.emptyparagraphkiller.status true); epk_off does not have the filter.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a text format with machine name 'epk_task'. Enable the Empty Paragraph Killer (emptyparagraphkiller) filter on that text format and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: filter.format.epk_task has filters.emptyparagraphkiller.status === true (the filter enabled on that format).

evals.prompt: My editors keep leaving blank empty lines in content. Create a new text format on my site called 'epk_new' that automatically strips out those empty paragraphs, using the module I installed for that. Make it live.
evals.expected_output: A text format 'epk_new' exists (filter.format.epk_new) with the emptyparagraphkiller filter enabled (filters.emptyparagraphkiller.status true).
